observations: Two solar panels standing upright on a concrete floor inside what looks like a shop or storefront.
Panels appear monocrystalline (dark blue/black cells with visible soldered tabbing, grid-like cell pattern).
No visible manufacturer logo, model plate, wattage sticker, or serial number on either panel in either photo.
A watermark reading 'YOUNG MIRACLE GLOBAL LINK' overlays photo 1, placed by the seller/platform, not the manufacturer.
Frames look aluminum, edges appear intact with no visible cracks, bends, or shattered glass.
Background shows a shop with boxed goods (possibly inverters/batteries) partially visible, consistent with a solar equipment dealer.
Cell grid can be roughly counted in photo 1: appears to be about 12 columns by 8 rows, consistent with a 96-cell layout.

claims.evidence: No brand name, logo, or country-of-origin marking visible in photo 0 or photo 1.
No rating/spec sticker or nameplate visible on either panel; wattage cannot be read from the photos.
Cell grid in photo 1 is roughly consistent with a 96-cell layout (approx. 12x8), but angle and partial framing make an exact count unreliable.
No visible cracks, discoloration, or hotspots in either photo, but surface condition alone does not confirm electrical performance.

risks.risk: Actual power output may be below the claimed 400W or panel may be degraded/non-functional from prior use.
risks.proof: A clip or photo of the panel connected to a multimeter/clamp meter under sunlight showing voltage and current output.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not confirmed working, i.e. at worst-case (non-functional/low-output) value

risks.risk: No manufacturer label means brand and country-of-origin ('Canadian') cannot be confirmed; could be a generic or rebranded panel.
risks.proof: A close-up photo of any rating plate, barcode sticker, or printed model/brand marking on the back of the panel.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unbranded generic panel, not as a premium-brand panel

risks.risk: Hidden micro-cracks or delamination common in used panels, invisible in standard photos.
risks.proof: An electroluminescence (EL) test image or close-up photos in bright even light from multiple angles, especially corners and solder joints.

risks.risk: Frame or junction box damage not visible from the front-facing angle shown.
risks.proof: Photos of the rear junction box and all four frame edges/corners.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming possible junction box or frame issues

proof_requests: Close-up photo of the rating/spec label or rear nameplate showing brand, model, and wattage.
Photo or short video of the panel's output reading on a multimeter under sunlight.
Close-up photos of the rear junction box and all four corners/edges for damage.
A clear, straight-on photo of the full cell grid to confirm exact cell count.
response.reason: The item is clearly identifiable by type as a used monocrystalline solar panel, but none of the seller's specific claims (brand, origin, wattage, working condition) can be confirmed from the photos, so it must be priced at the worst case for an unverified, unbranded, condition-unknown used panel.
